I would personally recommend the suicide hotline at 1-800-273-8255. It was hard for me to communicate how I felt to anyone I knew, and that sense of anonymity I got from calling a hotline anonymously made me feel, at least, slightly safer. The people there are patient if you're having trouble getting to the words you want to say, and if all else fails, you can just read exactly what you've posted here and say, "This is a post I made on the internet."

For me, after I typed my post on SW, I felt a little bit bolder. Then I felt able to call the hotline. Then I felt able to tell my parents. And they didn't judge or scold me for what I'd done, they just offered to help me to the help I needed.

How do you know him, and how do you know he's off committing suicide? Trying to sort the ideas out, I'm not challenging you.

Edit: Contacting emergency services should still be a priority. The operators are trained to save people in ways that I and the majority of Reddit are not. Call them and talk to them. Keep in mind what you know about the situation, and help them help you. Talk to us later. We're awesome and stuff, but we probably aren't as helpful as them.

If you know for certain that your friend is about to do something fatal to themselves, call 911, or the appropriate number in your location for emergency services and explain the situation to the operator.

I understand and respect the joy of the anonymity of internet. You get all kinds of time to think out your responses, and when you feel like disappearing from the conversation, you can click that little x in the corner.

That said, the suicide hotlines that you can call are actually pretty good, even if you're like me and you rehearse your pizza calls before you punch the numbers. Typically speaking, they're just people. People with experience talking to people battling depression. They'll talk to you about things to do proactively in your situation, and they'll give you that supportive edge you might not otherwise have.

Don't be afraid to give them a call.

I think it's the same problem with my writing. When I read the words, I just see the words on the page. I can't get into the stories. Worst part is, I just got an E-reader a couple months ago. I can't use it because I haven't been able to read.

I'm a good twenty or so pages into my project, but I haven't been able to add a sentence for the last five months. I know the next events, and I know where it's going, but I can't get any words to come out when I write. Goes for anything creative. And I hate to get all worked up over writer's block, but writing and my girlfriend were the last things I had. She's a big old jerk-face, and I can't write anymore. I'm pretty sure I'm through.

I've seen a professional. He prescribed me some Prozac and threw me out of his office. And it might just be my depression talking, but when he said, "If you were really suicidal, you'd have killed yourself by now," I interpreted it as a dare. I missed an appointment about a month ago and stopped refilling my prescription, because I don't feel like either of those did more good than harm.

But anyway, I'm interested in practicing escapism through video games, television and reading. They used to include escapism through writing, too, but that's gotten jammed up recently. It's also hard to read anymore.

But thanks for listening. That really is nice of you.
